summary: Revise at 6.7 (Caiman 7, ship bar 7.5). Face-on, the head now names the animal without a caption: a six-horn comb on the back edge, small domed eyes at the widest part, about eight fringe spikes down each flank, and a mirrored plate mosaic tapering to a blunt snout. The horn comb also gives a silhouette that no other Cataphracta or Reptilia ring has. The ring falls short in four places. (1) The sculpted head's finish is below the bar. Plate joints are serrated and stair-stepped, plate rims are frayed and crinkled, and there are two notched pits on the midline (stones.png, head.png). The snout-end wall of the head plate is a combed, vertically streaked cliff that hangs over the factory point (shoulder.png, stones.png, reverse.png). Both occipital horn tips are split, which matches the wall census's paper-thin zones (0.00004 to 0.0005 mm) at x ±1.6 to 2.0, y 14.4 to 14.9, z −7.5 to −8.6. (2) The head is a plate laid inside the shield, so a bare polished moat 1 to 1.5 mm wide runs round it, and the shield's flanks are bare mirror. (3) Away from the face, the theme falls apart into scattered granules. The shoulders, palm and reverse show sparse random dots in clusters on polished ground. The planned crest tubercle row (12 per side in the report) and the lateral fringe (2 per side in the report) do not read in any view. Density there is well below Caiman's and the Reptilia sheet. (4) The template gate in template-verification.json records template_gate_passed false (12.0 MB against the 3 MB painted budget). That file is dated 2026-10-03 18:15, before the current design (2026-10-04 02:21), and its triangle count (574,796) is not this build's (684,968), so it is stale as well as failed. The sand gates (ray release, clamp bites, two-part pull) are not applied, because Logan's 2026-10-03 ruling judges this ring as lost wax. The lost-wax gates in report.json all verify green. One round focused on the head finish, filling the moat, and a real shoulder-to-palm hide could plausibly reach 7.5.
strengths: Without a caption, face-300 reads as a horned lizard: horn comb with a midline notch, eyes on the widest part, flank fringe, mirrored plate mosaic and a tapering blunt snout.
The horn comb is a unique silhouette in Cataphracta and against the Reptilia tiles. The occipitals are now stout (1.17 mm root radius for 2.7 mm length) and swept back 34° with 12° to 25° of splay.
The plate mosaic has true hierarchy: large midline plates stepping to smaller flanking ones, mirror-true across the midline.
The flank fringe of 8 or so outward spikes per side, which read test 5 asked for, is there and countable in face.png.
Every lost-wax gate in report.json verifies green at the export build: watertight, 0 crossings on the ring and all 3 parts, Castable at 0.8 mm, 0 DFM, 0 vertices in the bore, cold reload identical.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: The theme is dense on the head but scattered everywhere else. The shoulders, palm and reverse carry sparse random granule clusters on polished ground (palm.png, reverse.png, side.png). No crest tubercle row or graded fringe reads on the shank, and the shield flanks and the moat round the head are bare mirror.

checklist.item: The hide reads as this animal at 300 px without caption
checklist.reason: In face-300 and hero-300 the head reads as a horned lizard: comb, eyes, fringe and tapering snout. The shank hide alone would read as generic pebbling, but the head carries the read.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing/smearing/stair-steps
checklist.reason: The horns and eyes are crisp, but plate joints are serrated and stair-stepped and plate rims are frayed (head.png, stones.png). Two notched pits sit on the midline (stones.png at about the upper third and the lower third). The snout-end wall of the head is combed with vertical streaks (shoulder.png, stones.png, reverse.png), and both occipital tips are split (face.png, stones.png).

checklist.item: Stones in made settings and visible
checklist.reason: Not applicable: no stones by design, and the report records 0 previewed and 0 reported.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: The plates are flat-topped faceted plateaus with triangulation streaks on their tops. The head is a slab dropped on the table with a vertical cliff at the snout instead of being blended into the shield, and the shank is untouched stock with dots stuck on.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The shield's back corners and side edges are kept, but at the point the head's snout wall overruns the factory edge. In shoulder.png and reverse.png a combed wall stands where the crisp shield point was (compare bare-vs-finished.png).

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from other Cataphracta rings and Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: The raised six-horn comb over a shield head is unlike Varanus, Ophidian or the bands, and unlike the other Cataphracta concepts.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The head has all three scales (horns, plates, eyes and fringe), but about 60% of the ring's visible area (shoulders, palm, flanks) carries only one scale of sparse dots on bare metal. Caiman and Varanus are covered face to palm.

Passes by its own definition, but census.clean is false. sampled_min is 0.00004 mm, and two edge zones of about 1 mm² each are 0.0005 mm thick at the occipital horn tips (x ±1.7 to 1.9, y 14.5 to 14.9, z −8.1 to −8.6), along with 4 'suspected artifact' walls at the same spot. The split tips in face.png and stones.png confirm these are real geometry, not noise.

gates.gate: template gate (<= 4 design.set patches within class budget)
gates.verified: template-verification.json records template_gate_passed false: 12,003,931 bytes against the 3,000,000 painted budget, 1 patch. The file also predates the current design (18:15 on 10-03 against 02:21 on 10-04) and records 574,796 triangles, not 684,968.

punch_list.zone: Horned head: the plate mosaic (all 75 plates), the joint grooves and the midline
punch_list.change: Rebuild the plate joints as clean, continuous V-grooves of 0.30 to 0.35 mm with smooth, single-curve rims, with no serration, no fraying, and no flat triangulated facets on the plate tops. Give each plate a gentle domed top (0.05 to 0.10 mm crown), not a flat faceted plateau. Fill the two notched pits on the midline (about one third and two thirds of the way down from the horn row) with whole plates.
punch_list.acceptance: In head.png and stones.png, no joint shows sawtooth or crinkled edges at full resolution, no plate top shows streaked facets, and the midline column is unbroken from horn notch to snout.

punch_list.zone: Horned head: snout end and the shield point (the head's lower edge in face.png, the cliff in shoulder.png)
punch_list.change: Pull the head's snout back at least 0.8 mm inside the factory shield point, and replace the combed vertical cliff with a drafted, smoothly fillet-blended skirt (0.3 to 0.5 mm radius) down to the table. Keep the factory point crisp, as in bare-vs-finished.png.
punch_list.acceptance: In shoulder.png, stones.png and reverse.png, no vertical streaking shows on any wall of the head. The shield point's hard edge is visible and unbroken in bare-vs-finished.png and shoulder.png.

punch_list.zone: Occipital horn pair, tips (x ±1.6 to 2.0, y 14.4 to 14.9, z −7.5 to −8.6)
punch_list.change: Close the split tips: give every horn a single solid tip with a radius of at least 0.25 mm and no seam or forked cap.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json wall_census shows no edge or wall zone thinner than 0.2 mm near the horn tips (suspected_artifacts empty there, sampled_min >= 0.2 mm in the head). In face.png and stones.png both occipital tips are single rounded points.

punch_list.zone: Shoulders, both sides (theta from the head's shoulders to about 100° past them), and the palm
punch_list.change: Replace the random granule scatter with an organised horned-lizard flank hide. Run a graded crest row of 10 to 12 round tubercles per side on the parting line, 1.2 mm grading to 0.7 mm, plainly visible. Give the shoulder walls the planned lateral fringe: pointed scales, at least 12 per side at the head end, grading palmward. Fill between them with close-packed granules (lands at most 0.5 mm, no bare metal larger than 1 mm across). Grade the palm to fine, close-packed ventral granules over the whole outer surface.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png, shoulder.png and side.png, a counted tubercle row and fringe read on each shoulder. In palm.png and reverse.png no polished patch wider than 1 mm shows on the outer surface, and the coverage at 300 px is as even as Caiman's or Varanus's shank.

punch_list.zone: Table margin between the head plate and the shield edge (the polished moat), and the shield flanks under the table
punch_list.change: Carry the head ground out to the shield edge. Fill the moat (1 to 1.5 mm, all round the sides and back) with a band of small granules or enlarged jaw-fringe scales stepping down to the factory edge. Pebble the shield's side flanks under the table with the same granules, so no mirror flat larger than 1.5 mm remains above the shank.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and hero.png no continuous polished border shows round the head, and in shoulder.png and side.png the shield flanks are textured up to the hard factory edge.

punch_list.change: Re-run the template gate on the current design, and bring the template within the painted budget (3 MB) or the class budget Logan accepts, with at most 4 design.set patches. Add the gate to report.json gates.
punch_list.acceptance: template-verification.json is newer than design.ring.json, its triangle count equals report.json build.triangles, template_gate_passed is true, and report.json gates lists the template gate as passing.

punch_list.zone: Horn comb at the hero angle (hero.png, hero-300.png)
punch_list.change: Strengthen the backward sweep so the comb reads as horns laid over the neck, not as an upright picket: raise the occipital rise from 34° to about 40° back from vertical, and the temporals from 30–32° to about 38°.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero-300 the horns visibly lean away from the snout and the outline no longer reads as an upright tiara.
